concept: SQL Server resumable online index operations
summary: Source-anchored research for SQL Server resumable online index operations. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Resumable index operations don't require a large transaction, which allows frequent log truncation during the operation and avoids large log growth. The data required to resume and complete the operation is stored in the database's data files. Resumable operations need additional log throughput during the sorting phase, although overall log space usage is lower than for a regular online index rebuild. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/indexes/guidelines-for-online-index-operations?view=sql-server-ver17 ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-index-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17

Use sys.index_resumable_operations to inspect state and percent_complete. Brent Ozar's reproducible 2020 demo shows that percentage can mislead when rows change during a pause; avoid treating it as a reliable ETA. (medium confidence)

Resumable operations preserve progress across explicit pauses, failures, and failovers. In a dbi services SQL Server 2017 experiment, killing the SQL Server process left the rebuild paused at 19% after service restart; ALTER INDEX... RESUME continued the operation. (high confidence) Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/indexes/guidelines-for-online-index-operations?view=sql-server-ver17 ; https://www.dbi-services.com/blog/sql-server-2017-whats-happens-with-an-interruption-during-a-resumable-online-index-rebuild/

Microsoft's July 2026 guidance says paused operations reject transactions needing table-level exclusive locks, including INSERT with TABLOCK, with error 10637; remove the hint or complete the operation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-20)

SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON is incompatible with resumable rebuilds; Niko Neugebauer reproduced error 11438 in a SQL Server 2017 CTP 2.0 build, and Microsoft's current ALTER INDEX reference retains the restriction. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-index-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17 ; https://www.nikoport.com/2017/04/23/resumable-online-index-rebuild/

Use ALTER INDEX <index> ON <table> PAUSE, RESUME, or ABORT to control a resumable operation. Cancellation or failure can leave resumable work paused indefinitely; explicitly ABORT it to discard the operation. Aborted work cannot be resumed. (high confidence)
The engine divides a rebuild into incremental units and persists continuation state, so interruption loses minimal progress instead of requiring a complete restart. (medium confidence)

Computed columns used as index keys can prevent resumable rebuilds, including implicitly inherited clustered-key columns in nonclustered indexes; inspect the effective key rather than only explicitly declared columns. (medium confidence)

Neugebauer's preview tests measured 65.8 versus 60.8 seconds on one table and 232 versus 230 seconds on a larger table; these tests excluded concurrent workload and do not establish production overhead. (low confidence)

The documented resumable rebuild restrictions exclude SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON, explicit user transactions, ALTER INDEX REBUILD ALL, columnstore indexes, filtered indexes, and disabled indexes. A maintenance script must check eligibility rather than apply resumability to every index. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-21) Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-index-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17

SQL Server introduced resumable online index rebuilds in 2017 and resumable online index creation in 2019. RESUMABLE = ON requires ONLINE = ON; an ordinary online operation is not automatically resumable. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-20)
Start a rebuild with ALTER INDEX ix ON dbo.t REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON, RESUMABLE = ON); control it with ALTER INDEX ix ON dbo.t PAUSE, RESUME, or ABORT. (medium confidence)
MAX_DURATION limits execution time in minutes before pausing. Cancelling or killing a resumable operation leaves retained work; ABORT explicitly discards it. (medium confidence)

A paused rebuild retains both index structures, consumes disk space, and continues to maintain them during DML. Write-heavy workloads can therefore pay overhead while the build is paused; pausing is not equivalent to releasing all resources. (high confidence)

MAX_DURATION on a resumable operation limits execution time in minutes before it pauses, allowing maintenance across multiple windows. RESUME can change MAXDOP. MAX_DURATION inside WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY instead controls lock waiting, so these settings have distinct purposes. (high confidence)

sys.index_resumable_operations exposes resumable operations and execution state. Redgate demonstrates monitoring percent_complete, state_desc, start_time, last_pause_time, and total_execution_time; dbi services uses the same view to inspect state after a server interruption. (high confidence) Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-index-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17 ; https://www.red-gate.com/simple-talk/sql/database-administration/resumable-online-index-create-and-rebuild-operations/ ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/system-catalog-views/sys-index-resumable-operations ; https://www.dbi-services.com/blog/sql-server-2017-whats-happens-with-an-interruption-during-a-resumable-online-index-rebuild/

Online index operations hold a shared (S) or schema modification (Sch-M) lock in the final phase, which can block other workloads, especially inside an explicit user transaction. Resuming a paused operation has to acquire the necessary locks. WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY lets the operation acquire low-priority locks and manage S or Sch-M lock behavior; ONLINE and RESUMABLE alone do not guarantee freedom from blocking. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/indexes/guidelines-for-online-index-operations?view=sql-server-ver17 ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-index-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17

Paul White reproduced a severe log-exhaustion/resume slowdown on SQL Server 2022 CU16 Developer Edition: a build taking about 78 seconds uninterrupted took 3 hours 19 minutes with repeated log-full pauses. This is a specific reproduction, not a general resumable-build performance estimate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-04)
